question: to the Commission Anna Maria Cisint (PfE) Subject:

The European Commission has recently recommended that Schengen States phase out all internal border checks, a stance that is blatantly at odds with the new Schengen Borders Code. One of the areas affected would be the Italian-Slovenian border, where checks were reintroduced in 2023 as a result of the major influx of migrants travelling along the Balkan Route. Yet, at the same time, the Union’s efforts to protect its external borders continue to be beset by major shortcomings, while the Balkan Route is still one of the main corridors used by irregular migrants heading for Europe and remains a major security concern for the regions where Italy, Austria and Slovenia share bi-national borders. Given the situation, it is completely illogical to ask Member States to stop using an instrument that has enabled national authorities to beef up checks and step up their efforts to tackle the criminal networks involved in migrant trafficking. In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission not think that asking Italy to divest itself of an effective control instrument is illogical, given that the Union remains incapable of fully securing its external borders?
What further measures could the Commission take to combat new illegal migration flows and criminal organisations operating along the Balkan route?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.7.2026) The Commission Opinion on the necessity and proportionality of the reintroduction of border control by Italy of 2 June 20261 stresses that the reintroduction of internal border control must remain a temporary and exceptional measure of last resort, subject to the rules of the revised Schengen Borders Code2. The European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) shows a steady decline in detected unauthorised border crossings, including along the Western Balkans Route3. Moreover, the use of alternative measures, such as cross-border police cooperation and information exchange are an efficient and effective means to ensure a high level of security. The Commission continues to work on the reinforcement of the management of the external borders, through the upcoming revision of the Frontex Regulation and the entry into application of the Pact on Asylum and Migration, which includes the screening of third country nationals at the external borders4. Member States along the Western Balkans route continue to strengthen their operational cooperation under a ‘whole of route-approach’. Member States should fully use existing mechanisms to enhance security and operational law enforcement cooperation. The European Multidisciplinary Platform Against Criminal Threats (EMPACT) has two Operational Action Plans dedicated to Migrant Smuggling and Human Trafficking5. The European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol) continues to target migrant smuggling along the Western Balkans route. The recently established European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling within Europol further strengthens EU-level operational and analytical support for Member States in dismantling high-risk migrant smuggling networks.
1 Commission Opinion of 2.6.2026 on the necessity and proportionality of the reintroduction of border control by

Italy at its land border with Slovenia in accordance with Article 27a(3) of Regulation (EU) No 2016/399 (Schengen Borders Code), 2.6.2026 C(2026) 3552 final. 2 Regulation (EU) 2024/1717 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2016/399 on a Union Code on the rules governing the movement of persons across borders. OJ L 2024/1717, 20.6.2024. 3 European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), Frontex: Irregular border crossings into the EU down 37% in the first half of 2026, 10 July 2026, available at: https://www.frontex.europa.eu/media-centre/news/newsrelease/frontex-irregular-border-crossings-into-the-eu-down-37-in-the-first-half-of-2026-Z5YoLp. 4 Regulation (EU) 2024/1356 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 introducing the screening of third-country nationals at the external borders and amending Regulations (EC) No 767/2008, (EU) 2017/2226, (EU) 2018/1240 and (EU) 2019/817.
